previewText: Put the Garden Hose to Bed Before a Hard Freeze, Lawrenceville's BOO Fest on Friday, October 23, and a quick Gwinnett and Barrow market check.

paragraphs: We are in the thick of October now. I picked draining outdoor faucets and putting hoses away for this week's homeowner tip because it is easy to put off.
If you are looking for something local, Lawrenceville's BOO Fest is on Friday, October 23. Thanks for letting me land in your inbox each week.

market.title: Gwinnett and Barrow County: September 2026 at a glance
market.source: Realtor.com Economic Research county inventory data
paragraphs: Homes in Gwinnett County spent a median of 57 days on the market in September 2026, 0.9% longer than a year earlier. About 27% of active listings had a price reduction.
Sellers in Barrow County added 198 new listings in September 2026, 16.5% more new listings than a year earlier, while 207 homes were pending.
The simple version for Gwinnett and Barrow County: buyers have more homes to compare than they did a year ago, so pricing and condition matter more than ever.
market.verificationNote: Source: Realtor.com Economic Research county inventory data, September 2026 (latest monthly release). Figures are countywide listing data, not closed sales.

rotatingFeatures.label: HOMEOWNER / SEASONAL HOME TIP
rotatingFeatures.title: Put the Garden Hose to Bed Before a Hard Freeze
rotatingFeatures.topic: draining outdoor faucets and putting hoses away
paragraphs: Georgia winters are mild most days, but one hard freeze can still catch a hose that was left connected. UGA Extension's home checklist includes draining outdoor faucets and hoses and storing them for winter.
items: Let the hose drain completely before coiling it.
Store it somewhere it will not sit in standing water.
If a spigot drips, make a note to have it repaired.
rotatingFeatures.closing: It takes about ten minutes, and your spring self will thank you.
rotatingFeatures.source: Source: UGA Cooperative Extension, Home Maintenance Checklist (C1082).

rotatingFeatures.label: LOCAL COMMUNITY EVENT
rotatingFeatures.title: BOO Fest in Downtown Lawrenceville
rotatingFeatures.availability: Friday, October 23, 2026, evening (starts at 6 PM); free
paragraphs: Downtown Lawrenceville's BOO Fest is a free, family-friendly Halloween evening on the Lawrenceville Lawn, Bicentennial Plaza, and South Clayton Street.
Expect costumes, a treat trail, food vendors, and a few friendly spooky surprises.
rotatingFeatures.closing: The event page lists a 6 PM start; check it before heading out for the final end time.
rotatingFeatures.source: Source: Downtown Lawrenceville, BOO Fest event page.
